The time it takes for garden compost to be ready depends on whether you are using a hot or cold compost heap. A hot compost heap is typically ready within 3 to 6 months, whereas a cold heap may take 6 to 12 months.

*   A hot compost heap takes 3 to 6 months to become ready [1].
*   A cold compost heap takes 6 to 12 months to become ready [1].
*   Turning the heap every few weeks can speed up the composting process [2].

Sources do not directly state how long a compost heap takes if it is not actively being turned, only that turning it helps speed up the process [2].

## Evidence
*   A hot compost heap is ready in 3 to 6 months [1].
*   A cold heap takes 6 to 12 months [1].
*   Turning the heap every few weeks speeds it up [2].

## Assumptions
*   The sources only provide timeframes for hot versus cold heaps, and do not provide a general timeframe for a standard compost pile.
*   I assumed that the difference between a hot and cold heap is determined by the rate of decomposition.
*   I assumed that "ready" means the compost is fully broken down and ready for use in gardening.
